t: You're at the site of the Queen's Hall, a concert hall that stood on Langham Place from 1893 until 1941. Thomas Knightley designed it, and it held about 2,500 people. It became London's principal concert venue. The hall had drab décor and cramped seating but superb acoustics. From 1895 until 1941 it was the home of the promenade concerts, founded by Robert Newman with Henry Wood. It became known as the musical centre of the Empire, and Debussy, Elgar, Ravel and Richard Strauss all performed there.
